The *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1) is a canonical Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna* division of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Structurally, it integrates the dyadic classifications (*duka*), beginning with root conditions (*hetuduka*), with the triad categories (*tika*) of the Abhidhamma analytical framework [SuttaCentral]. No separate English title or traditional alternative title is documented in the SuttaCentral record [SuttaCentral].
No curated historical parallels in other canonical languages are recorded for this text [SuttaCentral]. Nevertheless, automated analysis by DharmaNexus documents massive Pali-internal formulaic reuse, detecting 52,947 matching passages across 458 other Pali texts, reflecting the combinatorial matrix characteristic of the *Paṭṭhāna* [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual overlaps occur with closely related sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, particularly *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1; 5,131 matches, with segments such as §150.1_0–154.1 aligning with §107.1_0–110.1_2), *Hetugocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.2; 2,357 matches), *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1; 2,339 matches), and *Kusalattika, Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 4.2; 1,995 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, DharmaNexus computes cross-language phraseological alignments with Tibetan Abhidharma and scholastic works, including the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā* (D4092), the *Abhidharmakośaśāstrakārikābhāṣya* (D4091), the *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (D4054), and the *Yogācārabhūmi* (D4035) [DharmaNexus].
